title: CFD methods and algorithms review scorecard

points.title: Governing equations and nondimensionalization
points.notes: report.tex describes compressible equations; flux.hpp and lusgs_solver.cpp:422–497 implement conservative face and physical-time residual terms. Independent analytical verification was not performed.

points.title: Mesh import and unstructured geometry
points.notes: cgns_mesh.cpp:148–275 reads CGNS zones and connectivity and :324 handles TRI_3/QUAD_4; unsupported general MIXED elements and untested multi-zone variants limit confidence. partition.cpp constructs a METIS cell graph.

points.title: Conservative finite-volume residual
points.notes: lusgs_solver.cpp:422–497 assembles numerical face fluxes with equal/opposite cell contributions and adds BDF time terms; globally reduced residual norms at :500–517. No independent order verification.

points.title: Approximate Riemann flux and entropy fix
points.notes: flux.hpp provides Roe and Rusanov paths, selected by numericalFlux, with source positivity fallback. The delivered steady results are limited by low limiter cap, not proof of a broken flux.

points.title: Boundary conditions
points.notes: lusgs_solver.cpp:231–259 implements farfield, slip and no-slip wall states; :432 onward uses them for face fluxes. Surface rows show boundary velocity checks; no independent boundary test was repeated.

points.title: Second-order reconstruction
points.notes: lusgs_solver.cpp:262–300 gradients, :303–410 limiter and reconstructed states; steady metadata reports second-order stage with slope cap 0.1 after first-order startup. This materially limits spatial accuracy.

points.title: Limiter and positivity control
points.notes: lusgs_solver.cpp:303–396 bounds slopes and includes positivity fallback; wall/small-cell first-order behavior and steady cap 0.1 strongly damp reconstruction.

points.title: Viscous discretization
points.notes: flux.hpp:263–290 forms stress and heat flux, but lusgs_solver.cpp:1014–1046 integrates the full stress traction in viscous force, with no tangential projection. The rubric requires a tangential skin-friction split. Wall shear/drag accuracy is also materially limited.

points.title: Implicit steady march
points.notes: lusgs_solver.cpp:530–666 assembles approximate block Jacobian and SGS, with source time step controls and steady CFL cap 0.1. Independent solver-order study was not performed.

points.title: Transient BDF2 two-loop method (Re 200)
points.notes: lusgs_solver.cpp:480–497 adds BDF residual and :1500–1546 runs inner updates and shifts physical histories after a step. Re200 metadata gives dt=0.01, t=300, inner convergence fraction 0.9983; report admits strong raw frequency noise and diffuse wake. No unsteady rerun.

points.title: MPI partitioning and scalability
points.notes: partition.cpp:110 calls METIS; lusgs_solver.cpp:185–218 communicates halo state/gradients with sparse Alltoallv counts; np2/8 cylinder and np2/4/8 NACA continuation force comparisons are close, but no np1 result was delivered.

disqualification_flags.flag: Solver uses explicit time stepping only
Report claims second-order reconstruction or limiter that is disabled in production
metadata.json claims METIS/ParMETIS but code uses geometric split or full-state replication
Re 200 run reaches final time but misses inner target on most steps (failed transient solve presented as periodic)
Normal viscous traction mislabeled as skin friction
Surface no-slip rows are actually adjacent cell-center velocities without documentation
